category_title: Oppositional and boisterous students with disruptive behavioral reputations
minimal_context: The student is sitting on the carpet after lunch participating in a whole-class read-aloud discussion of Ereth's Birthday.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's start our read-aloud of Ereth's Birthday. Before we read the next page, Roger was just saying he didn't think the fisher deserved to get in that trap anyway.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's remember to raise our hands. In this next part of the story, Ereth calls someone a 'loudmouth lollie'.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Fidgeting and facing away) Loudmouth lollie! (Guffaws and looks around at the other students, making a funny face)

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Please sit still and listen. Now, what do you call it when an animal acts like a human—has human qualities like talking or playing music?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (In a sassy tone) Um, unnecessary? (Laughs loudly and makes another silly noise, hoping to enlist others in the silliness)

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: Let's start our read-aloud of Ereth's Birthday. Before we read the next page, Roger was just saying he didn't think the fisher deserved to get in that trap anyway.

STUDENT: He didn't get killed.

TUTOR: Let's remember to raise our hands. In this next part of the story, Ereth calls someone a 'loudmouth lollie'.

STUDENT: (Fidgeting and facing away) Loudmouth lollie! (Guffaws and looks around at the other students, making a funny face)

TUTOR: Please sit still and listen. Now, what do you call it when an animal acts like a human—has human qualities like talking or playing music?

STUDENT: (In a sassy tone) Um, unnecessary? (Laughs loudly and makes another silly noise, hoping to enlist others in the silliness)

task.content: Participating in a whole-class read-aloud discussion

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: Each time Mae pronounced one of Ereth’s phrases
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Edward would repeat it, guffaw, and look around, hoping to enlist others in the silliness. interrupted 17 times during a single read aloud to say something silly to another student, laugh loudly, or make a smart-aleck comment.
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: hoping to enlist others in the silliness

behavior_patterns.condition: When other students misspoke about something or were trying to collect their thoughts during discussions
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Edward was quick with a know-it-all correction
